findings.element: loading-slow, after a failed "Try again" — the static note .b-note and the visible live region .b-live (render-b.js ~line 1685 and the retry handler below it)
findings.problem: Press "Try again", wait for it to fail, and the screen reads, in three stacked paragraphs: "This is taking longer than it should." / "The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works." / "Still not arriving. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works." The second and third lines carry the identical ten-word clause, one line apart, both visible, both 13px, the repeat set in full white so it is the louder of the two. This is not a screen-reader duplicate — the retry live region is `p.b-live`, not the `p.b-live.b-vh` used elsewhere, so it paints. Verbatim self-repetition inside four lines is the cheapest thing text can do, and it happens on the one screen where a guest meets failure and forms a view of the company.
findings.fix: In the retry click handler in render-b.js, set the failed-retry announcement to "Still not arriving." and nothing more. The reassurance stays where it already is, in the static note above, which is the single statement of what is safe. The live region then adds only the new fact.

findings.element: The reversibility bar .b-undo — the `say:` arrays at render-b.js lines 749, 777, 809, 901, 1007, 1037
findings.problem: One node reports every change the owner makes, and it is the most-read sentence in the owner surface. It currently speaks in six wordings across three tenses and two voices: "Send the invitations moved 7 days later." (active past) · "Send the invitations is now hidden from guests." (present) · "Send the invitations is now shown to guests." (present) · "Renamed to Rehearsal dinner." (passive, and it names the new value instead of the moment) · "Send the invitations was removed." (passive past) · "A moment was added." (passive past, names nothing). Two of the six refuse to say which moment changed, so an owner who moved one thing and renamed another cannot tell from the bar what it is offering to undo. "Removed" also renames the action: the button says "Delete this moment". Six sentences from one mouth in one place is the one-grammar-per-fact defect landing on the product's own signature behaviour.
findings.fix: Rewrite all six on one pattern — subject, past passive, detail: "Send the invitations was moved 7 days later." · "Send the invitations was hidden from guests." · "Send the invitations was shown to guests." · "Send the invitations was renamed to Rehearsal dinner." (subject is the name it had before the edit) · "Send the invitations was deleted." (match the button's verb) · "A new moment was added." (the only line with no name available, because none exists yet).

findings.element: publish — the 48px h2.b-pressTitle (render-b.js ~1470) against the inert label "Sending comes next" beside "Copy the link" (~1500)
findings.problem: The headline is "Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July." Three hundred pixels below it, under the primary button, the page says "Sending comes next". Both are visible at once at 1440. If they have had it for twelve days, sending does not come next; it already happened, and the card to the left says so again ("79 days away when this was sent"). The code comment above the headline states the intent exactly — "The screen stops pretending this is a first send" — and the announcement string was already conditionalised for the same reason, but the inert label was left unconditional and now reintroduces the pretence the fix removed. A publish ceremony that contradicts itself in two type sizes is the credibility of the whole surface spent.
findings.fix: Gate `inert("Sending comes next")` on the same test that already switches the headline: render it only when `F.publication.state !== "published"`. When the plan is already live, render nothing there — the headline states the fact and "Copy the link" needs no chaperone.

findings.element: The project line in the owner and publish header — `h("span", { text: "one of three" })`, render-b.js line 492
findings.problem: "Mara & Finn ONE OF THREE" sits in the header of every owner screen and the publish screen; it is the string with the highest impression count in the product. It has no noun, so it reads as an ordinal — this is number 1 of 3 — rather than the partitive it means. owner-empty then prints the identical words beside a different project, "Aisling & Tom ONE OF THREE", and two things cannot both be the first of three: to a reader the product has just contradicted itself. The audience for this product has never used a project-management tool and will not reconstruct "one of three projects in this workspace" from three words with the subject missing. "three" is also a hardcoded literal in a master whose stated rule is that every number derives from one accessor.
findings.fix: Replace the literal with the noun the product already uses for the object, and derive the count: `"one of " + F.fmt.word(F.siblings.length + 1) + " plans"`, rendering "one of three plans". If no number-to-word helper exists, add one for 2–9 in fixture.js beside the other formatters.

findings.element: owner-flight after "Add a moment" — the row title and accessible name "Untitled moment" (render-b.js line 809 and the add handler), against the editor's label "What it is" and its placeholder "What is happening"
findings.problem: The owner's first creative act produces a row reading "Untitled moment", and the accessible name says "Edit Untitled moment. Saturday 25 July, in 9 days." It is the only default-software string in a document that otherwise says "We said yes", "Behind you", "Nothing is planned until 1 August" — the register drops from a wedding to a database in the one place where a new owner is most impressionable. The same empty field is then asked for twice in two grammars thirty pixels apart: the mono label above it says "What it is", the placeholder inside it says "What is happening". Three names for one unnamed thing, all in one panel.
findings.fix: Replace every occurrence of the literal "Untitled moment" (row title, accessible name, rename-undo fallback) with "Not named yet", set in the same ink as the placeholder. Delete the placeholder "What is happening" so the field is prompted once, by the label "What it is" directly above it.

biggestWin: The voice. Across thirteen states there is not one exclamation mark, not one Title Case button, not one word of jargon and not one default string that a framework wrote — the product says "moment", "the day", "the plan", "the link", "guests" and "behind you" and never wobbles. The refusals are the proof: an empty field answers "Type the day first. For example, 3 October 2026.", a bad string answers "That is not a date. Try 3 October 2026.", a past date answers "That day has gone. Pick one still ahead.", and the stepper at its limit answers "This is as near as it goes. Tomorrow is the soonest." Four refusals, none of them blaming the reader, each naming the way out, all four in the same mouth. Around them sit lines a studio would be pleased to have written — "It carries the day, the distance and the plan, and nothing else: no notes, no suppliers, no prices.", "You can turn the link off at any time. Anyone holding it then sees that it has ended.", "Nothing has been deleted." — and the unfurl frames the whole thing in a sender's own words, "Here is everything, love. It updates itself.", which is the single warmest and most confident string in the document. The palette is spent, not merely obeyed: indigo appears exactly twice per screen, on today and on what is next, and is entirely absent from ended, publish and unfurl, which is why it means something when it shows. What stands between this and 9.5 is not a build and not a different decision — it is one editor reading the whole document aloud in order, once. Five strings do not survive that reading: a failure screen that says the same sentence twice, a publish headline contradicted by the label under its own button, an undo node with six grammars, a header partitive missing its noun, and one row that still says Untitled. Half a day of copy editing, not a rebuild.
